title: Cross-stage microbatch steering and adaptive kernel routing to maximize NCCL overlap
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: On the current multi-GPU serving runtime we see sustained GPU stalls during prefill/decode transitions and large variance in decode p99s when model shapes and request mixes shift. Root causes identified in spikes: (1) monolithic microbatch placement that forces synchronized NCCL collectives across tensor/pipeline stages, (2) kernel selection that ignores per-microbatch sequence length and KV cache hotness, and (3) attention kernels that fail to exploit small-headed token windows for fused attention paths. Goals: design and implement a scheduler that (A) steers microbatches across stages to create opportunistic NCCL windows (overlap comms with compute), (B) adaptively selects attention kernels per microbatch based on shape+KV footprint, and (C) staggers prefill->decode handoffs to avoid global blocking. Success metrics: reduce end-to-end decode p99 by 30% on mixed-length workloads, increase sustained throughput by 18% on 8xA100 baseline, and reduce observed GPU idle time during prefill spikes by 25%.
implementation_notes: Design summary: (1) Rendezvous coordinator: lightweight cross-stage scheduler that tags microbatch tokens with a placement hint and target NCCL phase. It maintains a compact window buffer and issues steering decisions every scheduling quantum (~2ms). (2) Microbatch steering policy: maintain two priority lanes — latency-sensitive (low-seq) and throughput (long-seq). The policy opportunistically groups long-seq microbatches to form larger NCCL collectives while scattering short-seq items to earlier decode stages. (3) Kernel routing table: extend runtime kernel selector with microbatch metadata (seq_len, kv_bytes, head_count, rotary/rope). Selector returns a kernel id and expected compute/comm ratio; scheduler uses this to align compute/comm phases. (4) Attention optimizations: add a fused small-head attention path that packs QKV and applies rotary/rope transform inline, plus a tiled attention path for long sequences to reduce memory churn. (5) NCCL overlap: use asynchronous NCCL launches (separate streams) and explicit cudaEvent-based dependency points to allow later stages to commence independent compute while collectives finish. Fallbacks: if topology or memory pressure disallows overlap, degrade to current staging behavior.
test_plan: Phase A (lab): unit tests for kernel selector and steering simulation with a synthetic workload generator (varying seq_len mix). Phase B (integration): deploy to 4-GPU and 8-GPU test rigs with NVLink/PCIe topologies; run perf harness with real customer-like traces. Phase C (dogfood): enable behind feature flag for low-percentage traffic on staging clusters; monitor p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, CUDA stream contention, NCCL latencies. Benchmarks to capture: per-microbatch kernel choice distribution, average KV cache hits, overlap time fraction (comm overlapped with compute).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated runtime flag: scheduler=false by default. 2) Canaries: enable on isolated customer slices and internal staging for 2 weeks. 3) Monitor rollback triggers: >5% regression in p95 or any increased OOM/IPC drops. 4) Gradual ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 4 weeks with telemetry dashboards. 5) Post-rollout: run a 72-hour regression sweep across top-10 model shapes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: topology variance (NVLink vs PCIe) can change benefit profile; Mitigation: query topology at startup and switch scheduler mode to topo-aware or conservative.
Risk: additional CUDA streams and asynch NCCL can surface race conditions; Mitigation: add event barriers and aggressive stress tests; pair with kernel-level canary build.
Risk: kernel selector mispredictions cause oscillation in steering; Mitigation: add hysteresis and a lightweight online profiler to adjust weights.
Risk: increased code complexity may hurt maintainability; Mitigation: encapsulate steering in a single scheduler module with clear interfaces and extensive unit tests.
